question: The shortest distance measured from the initial to the final position of an object is known as ______
solution:
The correct answer is __**displacement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Displacement** is a vector quantity, which means it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• It measures the shortest distance from the initial to the final position of an object.
 
• Displacement is different from distance, which is a scalar quantity and measures the total path length traveled by an object without considering direction.
 
• It is important in physics because it provides information about the change in position of an object in a specified direction.
 
• Displacement can be positive, negative, or zero, depending on the direction of movement.
 
• In mathematical terms, displacement is often represented as a change in position, denoted as Δx in one-dimensional motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration**__

 __
 
• **Acceleration** is the rate at which an object's velocity changes over time.
 
• It is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.
 
• Acceleration can be caused by changes in speed, direction, or both.
 
 
 
• **Speed**__
 __
 
• **Speed** is a scalar quantity that refers to how fast an object is moving.
 
• It is the rate at which an object covers distance, measured in units such as meters per second (m/s).
 
• Unlike velocity, speed does not consider the direction of movement.
 
 
 
• **Velocity**__
 
 
• **Velocity** is a vector quantity that describes the speed of an object in a particular direction.
 
• It can be represented as the displacement divided by the time taken.
 
• Velocity is important in understanding the motion of objects in physics.
